the HT-29 human colon carcinoma cell line, when grown in DMEM-HT- 29, releases soluble products that suppress the afferent arm of delayed-type hypersensitivty and delay the rejection of Mc FiFi2s tumor cells in syngeneic mice.
DMEM-HT29 inhibits the afferent arm of delayed-type hypersenstivity against the Mc Fi Fi 2(s) tumor in vivo and also inhibits the rejection of Mc Fi Fi 1(s) tumors in vivo.
HT-29 cells secrete a factor that inhibits the development of delayed-type hypersensitivty and the rejection of tumors.

the development of a new method for the study of the role of the immune system in the development of the immune system.
a better understanding of the role of suppressor mechanisms in the regulation of immune response to tumors.
the study of the mechanisms of action of the suppressor factor secreted by HT29 colonic adenocarinoma cells.

HT-29 cells secrete a factor that suppresses the immune system.
the DMEM-HT- 29 product is a potent immunosuppressant that can be used to inhibit the afferent arm of the immune response against a tumor.

DMEM-HT29 inhibited the development of delayed-type hypersensitivty by inhibiting the sensitizing phase of the immune response.

the HT-29 cell line can be used to induce a strong immune suppressive response.
